newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE grains higher on quality fears, sterling.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE grains higher on quality fears, sterling.

text.p: LIFFE grains were mostly firmer as quality concerns drove old crop higher and currency helped the new crop, traders said.

July last traded two stg higher at 83.50, bolstered by worries that new crop quality may be adversely affected by the continued wet weather. "It makes the old crop look like something good to own," one trader said.
July volume was, however, a meagre nine lots.

November, with 188 lots, dominated the 275 lot total. It last traded 0.65 stg higher at 86.65 stg. The rise was a result of sterling's fall from its recent five year high against the mark, the trader said. The British currency fell by over 2.5 pfennigs from a high of 2.91.
The low futures volume was emulated by the physical market, country brokers said.
